Package com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest

Class MultipartFormData

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest.MultipartFormData
public final class MultipartFormData extends Object
Pure, dependency-free multipart/form-data request-body encoder (RFC 7578 / RFC 2046). Callers add text and file parts through a small builder-style API and then obtain the assembled body as a binary-safe byte[] plus the matching Content-Type header value.

No network and no file I/O: file contents are supplied by the caller as byte[], so the whole class is side-effect free and offline-testable.

Parts are serialized in the order they were added, each introduced by a --boundary delimiter line and terminated by the closing --boundary-- delimiter, with CRLF line endings throughout as required by RFC 2046.

Name escaping. Field and file names are emitted inside Content-Disposition quoted strings. Following the WHATWG HTML form convention, the three characters that would otherwise break the header — the double quote and the two line-ending bytes — are percent-encoded: " becomes %22, CR becomes %0D and LF becomes %0A. No other bytes are altered.

    • MultipartFormData

      public MultipartFormData(String boundary)
      Creates an encoder with a caller-supplied boundary. The caller is responsible for ensuring the boundary does not appear in any part content.
      Throws:

    • addFile

      public MultipartFormData addFile(String name, String filename, String contentType, byte[] content)
      Adds a file part.
      Parameters:
      name - the field name
      filename - the reported file name
      contentType - the part content type; null/blank defaults to application/octet-stream
      content - the raw bytes (copied defensively; null is treated as empty)
      Returns:
      this encoder, for chaining

    • getBoundary

      public String getBoundary()

      Returns the full Content-Type header value, e.g. multipart/form-data; boundary=....

    • build

      public byte[] build()
      Assembles and returns the complete request body as a binary-safe byte array. Repeated calls with the same parts and boundary produce identical output.
